---
title: "Research"
subtitle: "The methods I work on, and the questions behind them"
---

My work sits on the statistical side of clinical, neuroscience and psychiatric research. Most of my methodological interests come from problems that arrive through consultancy: a protocol that needs a defensible sample size, a device that has to be validated against a reference, a biomarker whose usefulness has to be put in numbers.

---

## Agreement and reliability

Comparing a new measurement with a reference standard, or with itself over time. Bland–Altman limits of agreement, intraclass correlation, Lin's concordance correlation coefficient, Krippendorff's alpha and test–retest reliability.

## Biomarker evaluation

Quantifying how well single markers and combinations of markers separate clinical groups. ROC analysis, cut-off selection, comparing correlated AUCs with DeLong's test, and cross-validated combined models.

## Study design and sample size

Sample size and power for randomised trials, including cluster, adaptive and sequential multiple assignment (SMART) designs, and for high-dimensional omics studies with false discovery rate control. Protocol review against SPIRIT. Tools I use include the R packages `pmsampsize` and `FDRsamplesize2`.

## Survival and categorical data

Kaplan–Meier estimation, log-rank and stratified log-rank tests, Mantel–Haenszel methods, logistic regression and the difference between odds and probabilities when reporting it.

## Latent variable methods

Structural equation modelling for psychosocial research, including mediation and moderation, model fit and estimation choices, and latent class analysis with cross-validation.

## Reproducible analysis and teaching

Analyses that can be re-run and checked, in R, Python, SPSS and Jamovi, and the teaching materials that help researchers who are not statisticians do the same. See [Teaching](teaching.qmd) and [Notes](notes.qmd).
